about.title: About the data
about.subtitle: What the series shows, and what it deliberately does not hide.

scale.title: 9.5 million rows, millisecond responses
scale.body: The route aggregates a fact table of 9,525,993 deliveries. The response comes from a materialized view (day × channel rollup), so the same query that would cost ~2s scanning the fact table returns in a fraction of a millisecond. The “via cache” or “conversion_daily” tag on the KPIs shows where it came from.

nullRate.title: A day with no sends has no rate — it is not zero
nullRate.body: Division by zero returns null, not 0. On the chart the line breaks; a false zero would look like a drop in performance that never happened.

rateAlone.title: The rate alone lies about WhatsApp
rateAlone.body: Email sends millions, WhatsApp sends thousands. A 100% rate on two sends is not a win. That is why sent and converted travel next to the rate on every row, and the “By channel” view gives each channel its own axis.

status3.title: Status 3 (Incomplete) does not exist in the data
status3.body: The spec lists six statuses; the dump ships five. That is why it does not appear among the conversion filters.

createdAt.title: The created_at field is synthetic and deterministic
createdAt.body: The dump has no timestamp column. created_at is generated from the id’s ordinal position through a seasonality curve — no randomness, the same dump always produces the same dates.
